requirements.actor: Any public visitor
requirements.trigger: The visitor opens /jw-stone or an existing JW profile destination
requirements.behavior: The new marketplace renders only at /jw-stone while existing JW profile and custom-domain destinations retain their current renderer and behavior.
requirements.constraints: The new route is standalone, reachable, canonical, and has no presentation migration or redirect from the existing profile.
requirements.negative: No code may switch, restyle, redirect, or mutate /u/jw-stone, the JW custom-domain profile, profile editing, inventory routes, or database presentation settings.
requirements.unchanged: All current JW profile appearance, behavior, editing, inventory, Direct Connect, and custom-domain routing remain unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Route and regression tests distinguish /jw-stone from every existing profile route and the rendered application confirms the separation.
requirements.proof: App routing tests, server route tests, profile regression tests, source diff review, and desktop/mobile route captures.

requirements.actor: Fabricators, builders, designers, and homeowners
requirements.trigger: A visitor begins discovery on /jw-stone
requirements.behavior: The visitor sees First Cut and real supplied catalog selections under the approved Current Inventory heading immediately, can open a stone in one click, and may independently choose a customer path, visual color direction, material, finish, search term, verified origin, or eligible named-stone detail through reversible shareable state.
requirements.constraints: Customer path and every refinement are optional and restore independently from clean public query parameters; invalid values do not discard unrelated valid state.
requirements.negative: No customer-path or color choice may gate inventory, replace the page, start a questionnaire, manufacture another choice, open contact, or expose price values or anonymous internal identifiers.
requirements.unchanged: Existing profile discovery and search behavior outside /jw-stone remains unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Tests prove initial inventory, one-click detail access, independent URL round trips, invalid-state recovery, and optional refinements without a staged dependency.
requirements.proof: State parser unit tests, component journey tests, and desktop/mobile browser journeys.

requirements.actor: A Fabricator, Builder & Developer, Architect & Designer, or Homeowner who wants targeted help
requirements.trigger: The visitor clicks one compact customer-path control
requirements.behavior: One in-place panel reveals concise source-attributed decision support and a compact rail of validated named JW stones selected by an explicit evidence-safe reason.
requirements.constraints: Guidance uses the exact sources and item rules in data-contract.md; recommended slugs are named, reviewed, catalog-valid, and capped at six; each rail and item shows its factual reason; the closed selector is one toolbar row and the complete expanded guide stays under 520 rendered pixels at 1440 and 390 widths; the complete storefront and its ordering remain present.
requirements.negative: A path cannot become a product, workspace, questionnaire, filter, page replacement, contact action, audience-specific catalog, or claim of suitability, popularity, live availability, future supply, origin, performance, or preference.
requirements.unchanged: Canonical inventory identity, shared cards, galleries, wishlist, filters, and optional Direct Connect boundaries are identical across customer paths.
requirements.acceptance: Focused tests and four browser captures prove exact source links, no more than three knowledge points, no more than six validated named stones, visible evidence reasons, a sub-520-pixel guide with no viewport/min-height styling, no second choice, and an unchanged ordered collection ID list before and after every path click.
requirements.proof: Workspace contract tests, DOM structure assertions, source review, and visual evidence for each buyer.

requirements.actor: Any marketplace visitor

requirements.negative: No invented name, material, finish, origin, dimensions, quantity, availability, translucency, exclusivity, geology, public price, or internal anonymous label may render or enter metadata, URLs, storage, analytics, or contact context.
requirements.unchanged: The canonical JW inventory module and all source IDs, slugs, images, and verified source facts remain unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Inventory integrity tests reconcile the current record totals, identities, named and anonymous treatment, forbidden labels, safe request labels, and absence of public price surfaces.
requirements.proof: Catalog projection tests, canonical inventory comparison tests, forbidden-string scans, and rendered named/anonymous evidence.

requirements.trigger: Canonical inventory supplies an explicit verified country-of-origin value
requirements.behavior: Verified origin appears on appropriate cards, details, designer selections, filters, and shareable state; absent origin remains completely hidden.
requirements.constraints: Origin requires an explicit country, a verified flag, and a source designation; filter options derive only from those values.
requirements.negative: The application never infers origin from names, imagery, quarry associations, descriptions, material type, or general Internet knowledge and never renders an empty or unconfirmed origin label.

requirements.trigger: The visitor saves, removes, reopens, clears, or returns to a named stone selection
requirements.behavior: A versioned local-browser wishlist stores stable eligible stone IDs, restores safely on return, shows a count and dedicated selection view, and remains separate from contact.
requirements.constraints: Storage is bounded, minimal, account-free, and resilient to unavailable, full, blocked, corrupt, stale, or removed entries.
requirements.negative: Anonymous items, duplicated facts, public price, automatic contact, email or phone gates, reservation language, and malformed data never enter or break the wishlist.
requirements.unchanged: Existing authentication, carts, profile state, and Direct Connect behavior remain unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Tests cover save, unsave, clear confirmation, refresh and return restoration, corruption, quota failure, unavailable storage, maximum size, removed inventory, and contact separation.
requirements.proof: Pure storage tests, component persistence tests, and a browser close-or-reopen wishlist journey.

requirements.constraints: Named stones support stable detail sharing and saving; anonymous presentations use only Call for availability where identity is needed and cannot be saved under an internal name.
requirements.negative: No public price, unsupported availability, synthetic identity, mouse-only gallery, incorrect image orientation, or forced contact may appear.
requirements.unchanged: Source image order and canonical inventory identities remain unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Card/detail tests cover named and anonymous paths, keyboard gallery navigation, save labels, safe inquiry labels, responsive structure, and forbidden copy.

requirements.negative: Saving never opens contact, no automatic message is sent, no hold or reservation is created, and anonymous internal names never enter the handoff.

requirements.actor: A homeowner, designer, builder, architect, or fabricator

requirements.actor: A visitor ready for manual TradeScout follow-up
requirements.trigger: The visitor deliberately opens and submits the existing TradeScout request flow
requirements.behavior: The request context contains safe stone identity, scene and application, measurements, texture crop/vein/scale, openings, seams, edge, waterfall, and a confirmation-required inventory note.
requirements.constraints: Existing Direct Connect validation, submission, retry, routing, and retention remain authoritative; opening the drawer sends nothing and all current inquiries route to TradeScout manually.

requirements.actor: A desktop or mobile visitor using touch, keyboard, assistive technology, reduced motion, or a browser without working WebGL
requirements.trigger: The studio loads, resizes, receives keyboard/touch input, loses a texture/context, or cannot initialize WebGL
requirements.behavior: The viewport-first layout remains operable and understandable, every essential non-camera choice has labeled controls, and an accessible measured summary plus retry survives rendering failure.

requirements.proof: Accessibility-focused component tests and exact-revision desktop/mobile/keyboard/failure captures.
